text:
I tried my revised inspection checklist on 24 components, and I think it made some defects easier to spot. We recorded 9 flagged components, but we have not checked every flag against an independent inspection.

Our trial was carried out by one inspector in one workshop. I would not claim that the checklist is more accurate yet, and we still need to see whether other inspectors get similar results.
review: Remove first person and conversational wording across both paragraphs.
Preserve 24 components, 9 flags, missing independent verification and single-inspector/site scope.
Do not turn easier detection into a demonstrated accuracy improvement.

text: We ran the new configuration for 45 minutes and saw about 8% less energy use. That sounds great, but our temperature readings bounced around more than before. We did not measure whether those fluctuations affected product quality, so I cannot say that the new configuration is better overall. We should test that tradeoff before recommending it.
review: Use neutral impersonal language and retain energy benefit versus temperature variability.
Preserve approximation, unmeasured quality effects and the conditional recommendation.

text: We didn't spot a difference between the two groups, but our sample was tiny, so we're not claiming they're the same.
review: Preserve the null finding, limited sample and explicit refusal to claim equivalence.

text: I used $r=0.42$ in the analysis described in \cite{nadir2024}. I think the association may be useful, but I cannot say it proves causation.
review: Use impersonal academic language and retain association versus causation and uncertainty.

text: The findings suggest a possible association; however, the observational design does not establish causality.
review: The passage is already academic. An unchanged answer is acceptable; preserve evidential caution.
